referents.why: 'they will go up': third common plural; the frogs (w4) are the subject of the weqatal.
'they will go in': the frogs again, the subject of the continuing weqatal.
'your palace': second person masculine singular in Yahweh's message, Pharaoh.
'your people': Pharaoh's people, in the message addressed to him.

links.why: then runs within a verse only; across the verse boundary it is not used.
a weqatal continues what it follows: the Nile teems, then the frogs go up.
a weqatal continues the frogs' movement into the houses.

groups.why: two clauses in a row, both acts of the frogs, each stating its subject only in its verb; recorded as a reading for review (R5).

none_fit.where: Exo.7.27#cl3 to cl0, across the verse boundary
none_fit.what: a declared act (I will strike the territory with frogs) and what it brings about (the Nile teems with frogs); result is defined only for a command and what it brings about.
